distinguishing_features: Uses a high-gradient magnetic field to physically capture paramagnetic/ferromagnetic iron and thorium-bearing particles rather than modulating operating points or dosing chemistry
Introduces no reagent dose and no filter media; separation is by magnetic force on the particles
Targets sub-50 µm fines/colloids via F = χV∇(B²)/2μ₀ exceeding hydrodynamic drag
Applies a physical solid-liquid separation mechanism to a rare-earth leachate stream, not a brine/digester/fluidized-bed scaling or agglomeration problem
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Remove fine iron-bearing and thorium-bearing particulate impurities from a rare-earth leachate stream without reagent addition or filter-media fouling/clogging
parsed.viable_reason: WHIMS/high-gradient magnetic separation is an established industrial unit operation, and the force-vs-drag estimate confirms magnetic capture of micron-scale magnetic fines is physically plausible at the stated scale.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art employs magnetic-force capture; applying high-gradient magnetic separation to this specific leachate purification problem is a genuine mechanism-class departure, not a routine parameter tweak of the cited arts.
